verifiedClaims.claim: Uninsured-motorist (UM) coverage under § 38-77-150 is mandatory; underinsured-motorist (UIM) coverage is offered and frequently stackable across vehicles on the same household policy.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: UM is mandatory (§ 38-77-150: no policy may be issued unless it contains UM at no less than the § 38-77-140 limits). UIM must be OFFERED at the insured's option (§ 38-77-160). Stacking is narrower than 'frequently stackable': § 38-77-160 provides that if the insured carries UM/UIM 'in excess of the basic limits', he 'is protected only to the extent of the coverage he has on the vehicle involved in the accident', and if none of his vehicles was involved, 'only to the extent of coverage on any one of the vehicles'. Stacking of basic-limits coverage from other owned vehicles is a case-law doctrine for Class I insureds, not a statutory grant.
verifiedClaims.note: Soften: 'underinsured-motorist (UIM) coverage must be offered, and in some circumstances UM/UIM coverage on other household vehicles can be stacked — the statute limits stacking when you carry more than basic limits, so the policy language decides.' Do not say § 38-77-160 authorizes stacking.

verifiedClaims.claim: UM/UIM stacking under S.C. Code § 38-77-160 is the recovery lever that closes the gap.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: See above: § 38-77-160 governs UIM and limits stacking above basic limits; it is not a stacking statute.
verifiedClaims.note: Suggested: 'UM/UIM coverage under S.C. Code §§ 38-77-150 and 38-77-160 — including stacking where the policy and statute allow it — is the recovery lever that closes the gap.'

verifiedClaims.claim: According to the South Carolina Department of Public Safety's most recent Traffic Collision Fact Book, Georgetown County recorded hundreds of traffic collisions in the latest reporting year, with a measurably higher injury rate per crash than the statewide average
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Book 2024 Edition (the most recent): Georgetown County recorded 1,484 traffic collisions in 2024 — 19 fatal, 31 serious-injury and 378 other-injury collisions — killing 20 people and seriously injuring 38. Injury collisions were 27.6% of the county's crashes (409 of 1,484) against 23.8% statewide (34,195 of 143,801), so the 'higher injury rate per crash' holds. Georgetown's VMT death rate was 2.355 per 100 million VMT. US-17 carried 629 of the county's 1,484 collisions (42%) and 6 of its 19 fatal collisions, with 6 killed and 12 seriously injured — more than any other roadway in the county. 'Driving too fast for conditions' was the most-listed contributing factor (438 listings, on 8 of 19 fatal collisions).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS, South Carolina Traffic Collision Fact Book 2024 Edition, Part VI (Georgetown County pages; county table)
verifiedClaims.note: 'Hundreds' undersells a four-figure count. Suggested: 'According to the South Carolina Department of Public Safety's Traffic Collision Fact Book (2024 edition), Georgetown County recorded 1,484 traffic collisions in 2024, 19 of them fatal, and US-17 alone carried 629 of those crashes and six of the fatal ones — more than any other road in the county. Injury crashes made up 27.6% of the county's collisions against 23.8% statewide.' 2023 edition for comparison: 1,507 collisions, 21 fatal, 22 killed; US-17 663 collisions, 8 fatal.
